## Detail

### `fbi-cde-api` — CDE Data API (unkeyed origin)

REST API exposing UCR summary, NIBRS-derived, arrest, homicide, hate-crime, use-of-force and law-enforcement-employment data. The cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST origin is the backend the CDE web application itself calls; it serves the identical routes with no API key and no advertised rate limit.

- **Publisher** FBI CJIS Division, Uniform Crime Reporting Program
- **URL** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST
- **Documentation** https://api.data.gov/docs/developer-manual/
- **Endpoint** `https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/{route}`
- **Access** rest_api · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 1985–2026 · **updated** continuous · **latest release** 2026-08-15
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain. No explicit license text is published.
- **Primary identifier** `ori9_nibrs`
- **Fallback** `https://api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde/{route}?API_KEY={key}` (HTTP 200) — 403 without a key. Rate limits are hourly and per key; a newly issued key was observed at 10 requests/hour, standard keys at 1000/hour.

**Known limitations**

- Undocumented and unversioned; the LATEST path segment changes on redeploy.
- No OpenAPI specification exists; the endpoint catalog was reverse-engineered.
- No SLA or deprecation notice. A keyed api.data.gov fallback is configured.

### `fbi-cde-agency-directory` — Agency (ORI) directory

The live universe of ORIs enrolled in the UCR program, with agency name, agency type, county name and a point coordinate. The only current, machine-retrievable national agency list that needs no human login.

- **Publisher** FBI CJIS Division
- **URL** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/agency/byStateAbbr/{STATE}
- **Documentation** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/
- **Access** rest_api · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2026–2026 · **updated** continuous
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `ori9_nibrs`

**Known limitations**

- No national bulk endpoint; one request per state (56 including territories).
- No FIPS place code. County NAME only, and multi-county agencies appear under composite keys such as "KENT, SUSSEX" and "UNMAPPED COUNTY".
- No personnel counts.
- Reflects UCR enrollment, which includes agencies that never submit data.
- An ORI is a reporting identifier, not an agency. One agency can hold several.

### `fbi-nibrs-agencies` — agencies.csv (agency dimension inside each NIBRS state ZIP)

A 59-column agency-year table shipped inside every NIBRS state ZIP. The only published source carrying BOTH the NIBRS ORI9 and the legacy ORI9, which makes it the platform's identifier bridge. Also carries employment counts, participation flags, dormancy, population group, MSA, and the covered_by_legacy_ori parent pointer.

- **Publisher** FBI CJIS Division
- **URL** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/s3/signedurl?key=nibrs/incident/{year}/{ST}-{year}.zip
- **Documentation** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads
- **Access** bulk_zip · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 1991–2025 · **updated** annual
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `ori9_nibrs`
- **Ingestion note** The platform reads the ZIP central directory over HTTP range requests and fetches only the agencies.csv member, turning a ~2 GB national download into roughly 40 MB.

**Known limitations**

- One ZIP per state per year; California 2025 is 117 MB, Texas 116 MB.
- Presigned URLs expire after 900 seconds; sign immediately before each fetch.
- Covers NIBRS-participating agencies, so coverage tracks the onboarding curve.

### `fbi-ucr-pe-master` — pe-{year}.zip

Fixed-width agency-year employment file, LRECL 7689, keyed on ORI7. Sworn and civilian counts by sex, population served, and officer/employee rates per 1,000.

- **Publisher** FBI CJIS Division
- **URL** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/s3/signedurl?key=master_files/pe/pe-{year}.zip
- **Access** bulk_zip · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 1991–2024 · **updated** annual
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `ori7`

**Known limitations**

- pe-2025.zip downloads successfully and is ZERO-FILLED: 26,288 records, every employment count 0. Bulk PE is trustworthy only through 2024. A load-time assertion rejects any PE year whose total employees sum to zero.
- Keyed on ORI7. The correct bridge is legacy_ori[:7], NOT ori[:7]; deriving ORI7 from the NIBRS ori drops agencies whose forms differ in positions 7-9.
- Carries a larger, partly historical universe than the live directory.

**Coverage Measured**

- `2024`: {'records': 26136, 'with_employment_data': 15022, 'sum_total_employees': 1135770}
- `2025`: {'records': 26288, 'with_employment_data': 0, 'sum_total_employees': 0}

### `fbi-ucr-summarized` — Summarized crime time series

Monthly counts, rates and clearances for Part I offenses at national, state and agency level. Date parameters are MM-YYYY; a bare YYYY returns HTTP 400.

- **Publisher** FBI CJIS Division
- **URL** https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/summarized/{level}/{key}/{offense}
- **Access** rest_api · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 1985–2025 · **updated** monthly
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `ori9_nibrs`

**Known limitations**

- Twenty states no longer submit SRS at all (AR CO DE ID IA KY MI MT NV NH NC ND RI SC SD TN VT VA WV WY). This is structural, not a lag, and will not backfill.
- 2026 is fractional. National monthly violent-crime offenses fall from 87,397 in Dec 2025 to 42,498 in Jul 2026 to 4,696 in Aug 2026. The platform sets a hard cutoff at 2025-12 for any level or year-over-year comparison.
- The 2021 SRS-to-NIBRS transition leaves roughly 31% of agencies without 2021 data. Several FBI CIUS table families skip 2021 entirely.

### `bjs-csllea-2018` — Census of State and Local Law Enforcement Agencies, 2018

A complete enumeration of publicly funded state, county, local, tribal and special-jurisdiction agencies employing at least one FTE sworn officer with general arrest powers. The best statistical universe available, and the platform's reconciliation benchmark for agency counts.

- **Publisher** US DOJ, Office of Justice Programs, BJS
- **URL** https://bjs.ojp.gov/data-collection/census-state-and-local-law-enforcement-agencies-csllea
- **Documentation** https://bjs.ojp.gov/library/publications/census-state-and-local-law-enforcement-agencies-2018-statistical-tables
- **Endpoint** `https://bjs.ojp.gov/media/67831/download`
- **Access** bulk_zip · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2018–2018 · **updated** irregular (1992, 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2018; 2014 failed; 2022 unreleased) · **latest release** 2022-10-19
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `none (aggregate tables); BJS agency ID in the microdata`

**Known limitations**

- Only the AGGREGATE publication tables are script-downloadable. Agency-level microdata sits on ICPSR behind a login, and ICPSR returns 403 to browserless clients. No unattended refresh is possible.
- Published universe is eight years stale; the 2022 wave was fielded but not released.
- Excludes agencies below one FTE sworn officer, and excludes federal agencies.
- Publication tables carry an 8-row metadata preamble and a two-tier merged header.

**Headline Figures**

- `agencies_total`: 17541
- `local_police`: 11824
- `sheriffs_offices`: 3051
- `special_jurisdiction`: 1753
- `constable_marshal`: 647
- `tribal`: 217
- `primary_state`: 49
- `full_time_sworn`: 787565

### `bjs-leaic-2012` — Law Enforcement Agency Identifiers Crosswalk, United States, 2012

The only federally published ORI-to-FIPS/Census-government crosswalk. Contains ORI codes with FIPS state, county and place codes plus Governments Integrated Directory identifiers.

- **Publisher** US DOJ / BJS, archived at NACJD/ICPSR
- **URL** https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/NACJD/studies/35158
- **Documentation** https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/law-enforcement-agency-identifiers-crosswalk-united-states-2012
- **Access** manual_download · **verified HTTP** 403
- **Coverage** 2012–2012 · **updated** discontinued · **latest release** 2018-09-18
- **Licence** Public; ICPSR terms of use apply on download
- **Primary identifier** `ori`
- **Decision** Because this crosswalk is both auth-gated and stale, the platform BUILDS its own ORI-to-geography resolution and treats every link as a scored, reviewable artifact with its own provenance. See docs/methodology.md.

**Known limitations**

- Reference year 2012, fourteen years stale, with no successor announced. The 2018 "update" was a title typo correction, not a data refresh.
- Requires an ICPSR account; the CDN returns 403 to non-browser clients.
- ICPSR publishes no variable-level metadata for this series.

### `census-gazetteer-2025` — 2025 U.S. Gazetteer Files

Table of record for geographic identifiers, names, land/water area and internal points at every summary level. The platform's county and place dimension.

- **Publisher** US Census Bureau, Geography Division
- **URL** https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/gazetteer/2025_Gazetteer/
- **Documentation** https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/technical-documentation/records-layout/gaz-record-layouts.html
- **Access** bulk_zip · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2025–2025 · **updated** annual · **latest release** 2025-09-08
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `geoid`

**Known limitations**

- Format break: 2023 and 2024 are TAB-delimited; 2025 is PIPE-delimited and adds a GEOIDFQ column. A parser pinned to the 2024 layout silently produces one-column rows.
- Column sets differ between summary levels within the same year.
- INTPTLAT/INTPTLONG are internal points, not population-weighted centroids.

### `census-pep-2025` — Vintage 2025 Population Estimates

Modeled annual population for July 1 of each year, benchmarked to the 2020 Census. The platform's PRIMARY rate denominator, because a 2025 crime count divides by a 2025 population.

- **Publisher** US Census Bureau
- **URL** https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2025/
- **Documentation** https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html
- **Access** bulk_csv · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2020–2025 · **updated** annual
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `state_fips + place_fips`

**Known limitations**

- Total population only; no age, race, sex or income at place level.
- Vintages are not a time series. Each vintage re-estimates all prior years, so V2025 POPESTIMATE2023 differs from V2024 POPESTIMATE2023.
- No margins of error are published; uncertainty is real but unquantified.
- SUMLEV is load-bearing. 162 rows are incorporated places; 061 rows are minor civil divisions and will double-count against place rows in the same file.
- No place-level PEP is available from the Census API; bulk CSV only.

### `census-acs5-2024` — ACS 5-Year Estimates, Detailed Tables (2020-2024)

Period estimates pooling 60 months of responses, published to block group. The platform's SECONDARY denominator and its only source of demographic composition.

- **Publisher** US Census Bureau
- **URL** https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5
- **Documentation** https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/acs-5year.html
- **Endpoint** `https://api.census.gov/data/{vintage}/acs/acs5?get={vars}&for={geo}&in={parent}&key={key}`
- **Access** rest_api · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2009–2024 · **updated** annual · **latest release** 2026-01-29
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `geoid`

**Known limitations**

- An API key is now MANDATORY; keyless requests return 302 to missing_key.html.
- A period estimate. The "2024" label spans 2020-2024, an effective midpoint of mid-2022, so it lags a real 2024 denominator by roughly two years.
- place requires in=state:; there is no national for=place:*. A national pull is 51 calls.
- Margins of error are large for small places and must be carried through.

### `census-urban-areas-2020` — 2020 Census Urban Area list and relationship files

2,645 urban areas defined from 2020 Census blocks by housing-unit density, with crosswalks to place and county. Supplies the platform's urbanicity band, which is a required peer-cohort dimension.

- **Publisher** US Census Bureau, Geography Division
- **URL** https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/ua/2020_Census_ua_list_all.xlsx
- **Documentation** https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/guidance/geo-areas/urban-rural.html
- **Access** bulk_xlsx · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2020–2020 · **updated** decennial
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `uace`

**Known limitations**

- In the place relationship file, rural places have all seven UA fields EMPTY. That is the rural signal, not a parse error.
- Places split across urban and rural appear on multiple rows; aggregating without deduplicating on GEOID_PLACE_20 inflates counts.
- UACE is a 5-digit national code with no state prefix; zero-pad it.

### `census-gov-finance-2024` — Individual Unit File (Public Use Format), FY2024

Record-level fixed-width file, one row per government unit per item code, in thousands of dollars. Item code E62 is police-protection current operations.

- **Publisher** US Census Bureau, Governments Division
- **URL** https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/gov-finances/tables/2024/2024_Individual_Unit_Files.zip
- **Documentation** https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/gov-finances/tables/2024/2024_methodology.pdf
- **Access** bulk_zip · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2024–2024 · **updated** annual; full universe in years ending 2 and 7 · **latest release** 2026-07
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `census_gov_id_12`

**Known limitations**

- The unit of observation is a GOVERNMENT, not a police agency. No Census-to-ORI crosswalk exists anywhere. The platform never publishes a per-agency spending figure.
- A voluntary stratified SAMPLE. 2024 covers 57.8% of counties, 20.8% of municipalities and 4.9% of townships, and 26.5% of E62 values are imputed.
- Survey year N spans fiscal years ending 1 Jul N-1 to 30 Jun N. 62% of units close 06-30, 17% close 12-31. Crime data is calendar-year.
- Employer pension contributions are EXCLUDED from E62 for a government running its own pension fund, and INCLUDED for one enrolled in a state system. Nothing in the file flags which regime applies.
- Contract policing is reported as direct E62 by the purchasing city and also sits in the providing county's total. Never sum a county and its cities.
- F62 is CONSTRUCTION. G62 and K62 have zero records in the public-use file.
- Files are revised silently in place; the 2022 file was reprocessed in July 2026.

**Coverage Measured**

- `e62_records_2024`: 5931
- `e62_imputed_2024`: 1569
- `e62_records_2022_census_year`: 19711

### `census-gus-2025` — 2025 Government Units Listing

Directory of all US governments with CENSUS_ID_PID6 and FIPS_STATE/COUNTY/PLACE. Used to validate the FIPS place crosswalk that ships inside the finance file.

- **Publisher** US Census Bureau, Governments Division
- **URL** https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/gus/datasets/2025/gov_units_2025.zip
- **Access** bulk_zip · **verified HTTP** 200
- **Coverage** 2025–2025 · **updated** irregular
- **Licence** US Government work, public domain
- **Primary identifier** `census_id_pid6`

**Known limitations**

- CENSUS_ID_GIDID (the 14-character ID) is present in the 2022 listing and DROPPED from 2025. Never key on it.
- The 2025 general-purpose universe is 38,704 units - 3,031 counties, 19,489 municipalities and 16,184 townships.

## Evaluated and deliberately not ingested

A dataset enters the production platform only when its source is defensible, its methodology is understood, its identifiers reconcile, and it adds analytical value the platform does not already have. These did not clear that bar for Phase 1.

### `bjs-lemas-2020`

A stratified SAMPLE of general-purpose agencies, not a census, so it cannot serve as an agency universe. Microdata is ICPSR-gated. Valuable for Phase 4 policy attributes with weights carried through, not for the Phase 1 spine.

### `bjs-lear-2016`

ORI- and FIPS-keyed and therefore tempting, but covers only general-purpose agencies (15,810, missing ~2,600 special-jurisdiction, tribal and constable agencies), is ten years old, was superseded by CSLLEA 2018, and was built partly on the failed 2014 CSLLEA. Historical provenance only.

### `fbi-use-of-force`

Participation is roughly half of agencies (Alaska 2024: 24 of 47). National counts are not national totals. Requires a participation-adjusted presentation before it can be shown honestly.

### `municipal-open-budgets`

Department-level appropriations are better attributed than Census function codes, but each portal has its own chart of accounts. Cross-city comparison needs a normalization layer that is out of scope for Phase 1. Eight Socrata portals are the natural start.
